previewHint: The plant registry is a preview in this version: its pages and the import format can still change.
notInSourceHint: An import replaced the one this entry came from, and its files no longer contain it. It was kept and marked.

form.name: Name
form.idHelp: Stable: lower-case letters, digits, “.”, “_” and “-”. Imports and links use it; it never changes.
form.idInvalid: Use lower-case letters, digits, “.”, “_” and “-”, starting with a letter or digit.
form.geoBoth: Give latitude and longitude, or neither.

sites.description: The sites of the enterprise with their hierarchy (ISA-95) and buildings.
sites.descriptionOf: The sites of {{enterprise}} with their hierarchy (ISA-95) and buildings.
sites.emptyText: A site is a factory of the enterprise. Add one by hand, or import the YAML files you keep elsewhere.

site.positionHelp: Optional: where the site is, for the link to OpenStreetMap.
site.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}} with its hierarchy and buildings? A site with assets cannot be deleted.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.name: Name
contacts.invalid: Each contact needs a name; check the e-mail addresses.

refs.title: External references
refs.help: The ids of this entry in other tools: an ERP equipment number, an asset id in another inventory.
refs.invalid: Each reference needs a system and an id; links start with http:// or https://.

hierarchy.title: Hierarchy
hierarchy.help: What happens where, after ISA-95: areas hold work centers (lines, cells), work centers hold work units. Each part names its building; the innermost one applies.
hierarchy.emptyText: Start with the areas of the site, e.g. machining or assembly.
hierarchy.whoCanAct: Whoever manages the site adds its hierarchy.

help.area: An area says what happens (machining, assembly, utilities) – not where. Put the hall in “Building”.
help.work_center: A work center is a line, unit, cell or storage zone of its area.
help.work_unit: A work unit is one place in a work center: a cell, a station, a rack.

node.domainHelp: Optional: the manufacturing domain of the area
node.buildingHelp: Optional: the building it stands in
node.deleteConfirm: Remove {{type}} {{name}}? Only empty parts can be removed.

buildings.help: Where things are: buildings, halls, floors and outdoor areas – apart from what happens there.

building.help: A place on the spatial axis. A floor or room names the building it is in.
building.parentHelp: Optional: the building this one is part of
building.deleteConfirm: Remove {{name}}? Only buildings nothing names can be removed.

assets.description: Machines and equipment of the sites you may see, with where they stand.
assets.search: Search name, id, model or tag
assets.place: Area, work center or work unit
assets.emptyText: Assets are the machines and equipment of a site. Add one on a site's page or here, or import them.
assets.clearDataPoint: Show all assets with this profile

asset.place: Area, work center or work unit
asset.placeHelp: The innermost place: the levels above follow from it
asset.buildingHelp: Optional: only when it differs from its place's
asset.parentHelp: Optional: the asset this one belongs to (same site)
asset.equipmentHelp: The asset this one is part of, and the assets that are part of it.
asset.hidden: In a site you may not see
asset.imageNotUploaded: The source names the image {{name}}; it is not uploaded.
asset.imageHelp: PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most {{kb}} KB.
asset.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}}? Its links and image go with it.
asset.deleteConfirmChildren: Delete {{name}}? Its links and image go with it; its {{count}} parts stay, without a parent.

source.title: Source
source.perEntry: An import keeps its files, not which file each entry came from.

import.title: Import YAML
import.description: Add sites, their hierarchy, buildings and assets from YAML files – one per site, assets apart, or a whole tree. You see what changes before anything is saved.
import.notAllowedText: Importing needs the right to manage a site or to add sites.
import.filesHelp: YAML or JSON in the plant registry format (version 1, see docs/PLANT.md). Several files are imported together.
import.tooLarge: The files are too large together (at most {{mb}} MB).

add.title: Add only
add.text: New entries are added; entries that are there already stay as they are.

update.title: Add and update
update.text: New entries are added, existing ones get what the file says. Keys the file leaves out keep their values.

replace.title: Replace an earlier import
replace.text: The files become the truth for an earlier import: its entries are written in full, and those the files no longer have are removed or kept and marked.

import.replacesHelp: Its entries that are not in the files any more are removed or marked. Entries made in Steward stay.
import.missing: Records of that import that the files no longer have
import.removeConfirm_one: The import removes {{count}} entry. Import anyway?
import.removeConfirm_other: The import removes {{count}} entries. Import anyway?

notes.markedHolds: Kept, marked “not in source” – it still holds entries
notes.namesRemoved: Names an entry that is removed

import.checksHelp: What Steward finds in the entries of the files once they are imported. These do not stop the import.

settings.title: Plant registry
settings.description: The sites of the enterprise, their ISA-95 hierarchy (area, work center, work unit), buildings and assets – with YAML import and export. A module of its own: off, nothing of it shows, and the rest of Steward works as before.
settings.enabledHelp: Adds the Plant area to the sidebar and sites and assets as link targets. Turning it off hides it again; its data is kept.
settings.turningOff: Off, the plant registry's pages, routes and links are hidden. Its data is kept and comes back when it is turned on again.
settings.enterpriseHelp: The name of the enterprise this installation documents (the root of the export)
settings.labelsHelp: Your own words for the entry types, e.g. “Machine” instead of “Asset”. Empty: the standard word.
settings.fieldsHelp: Fields of your own per entry type, checked on every save and import. In the import file they are under “fields:” with their key.

profiles.title: Device profiles
profiles.description: Kinds of controllers and devices with their interfaces and data points – one catalogue for every site. An asset names its profile.
profiles.emptyText: A device profile says which interfaces a kind of device has (OPC UA, Modbus/TCP, MQTT, file transfer …) and which data points they deliver. Add one, or import YAML files.
profiles.whoCanAct: Designers and administrators add device profiles and KPI definitions.

profile.versionHelp: The firmware or product version the profile describes, e.g. 2.x or any
profile.categoryHelp: e.g. CNC controller, power meter, robot controller
profile.interfacesHelp: How the device is read or written: each interface with its data points in groups.
profile.noKpis: No KPI definition reads this profile.
profile.deleteConfirm: Delete the device profile “{{name}}” with its interfaces and data points?

data.directionHelp: Seen from whoever reads the device
data.clientHelp: A gateway, a driver, a browser or “manual”
data.removeInterfaceConfirm: Remove the interface “{{name}}” with its {{count}} data points?
data.noInterfacesText: Add the interfaces of the device – OPC UA server, Modbus/TCP, MQTT, a file share, a web page – and then their data points.
data.removePointConfirm: Remove the data point “{{name}}”? KPI instances that read it show a problem afterwards.
data.groupHelp: Data points of an interface in groups (machine state, energy …); empty: without a group
data.groupTaken: The interface has a group of this name already.
data.nameIdHelp: Stable: letters, digits, “.”, “_” and “-”. KPI definitions, overrides and imports use it; it never changes.
data.nameIdInvalid: Use letters, digits, “.”, “_” and “-”, starting with a letter, digit or “_”.
data.dataTypeHelp: OPC UA type (Boolean, Int32, Float, Double, String …) or IEC 61131-3 type (BOOL, INT, REAL …); [] for an array
data.dataTypeInvalid: Use an OPC UA or IEC 61131-3 data type, or int, float, bool, string.
data.unitHelp: A UCUM code: kW.h, Cel, /min, % – kWh or °C are read as their code

addressHelp.opc_ua: OPC UA NodeId, e.g. ns=2;s=Spindle.Speed or ns=2;i=1001
addressHelp.modbus_tcp: Table, 0-based address and count: holding:100, input:7,2 (coil, discrete, input, holding)
addressHelp.other: A path, a file name or column, a URL …

data.addressOpcUa: Use the OPC UA NodeId notation, e.g. ns=2;i=1001 or ns=2;s=Spindle.Speed.
data.addressModbus: Use table:address,count – table coil, discrete, input or holding, e.g. holding:100 or input:7,2.
data.enumValuesHelp: The values a state or code can have, in their order
data.defaultPublicationsHelp: Where this data point is usually published; each asset says where it really is.
data.pathHelp: A path, an aspect, a topic

point.deliveredHelp_one: {{count}} of {{total}} assets with this profile delivers it: its interface is set up and active, and no override says it lacks it.
point.deliveredHelp_other: {{count}} of {{total}} assets with this profile deliver it: their interface is set up and active, and no override says they lack it.
point.noKpis: No KPI definition reads this data point.

kpis.title: KPI definitions
kpis.description: Key performance indicators computed from the data points: their inputs, parameters and result columns – one catalogue for every site.
kpis.emptyText: A KPI definition says which data points a computation reads, which parameters it takes and which columns it writes. Assets then get KPI instances of it.

kpi.formulaHelp: How the value is computed, e.g. availability_pct = running / planned_production_time × 100
kpi.rangeInvalid: The lowest value is above the highest.
kpi.strategyHelp: The computing system’s name of the method
kpi.implementationHelp: A repository path or a job type
kpi.dynamicColumns: The columns vary from run to run
kpi.dynamicColumnsHelp: The list below names the fixed ones; ratios are not checked against it.
kpi.dynamicColumnsNote: The columns vary from run to run; these are the fixed ones.
kpi.inputsHelp: The data points the computation reads. An asset can have the KPI when it delivers all of them.
kpi.profileHelp: Empty: the data points of whatever profile the asset has
kpi.parametersHelp: What a KPI instance may set; other spellings are aliases.
kpi.paramTaken: {{name}} is a name or alias of another parameter already.
kpi.aliasesHelp: Other spellings of the same parameter
kpi.requiredHelp: A KPI instance must set it when there is no default.
kpi.columnsHelp: What each run writes. Sums add up over a longer period; ratios are their numerator divided by their denominator, both summed first.
kpi.columnTaken: The definition has a column of this name already.

columnKindsHelp.ratio: Numerator / denominator × scale – both columns are summed first
columnKindsHelp.ignore: Descriptive: not combined over a period

kpi.scopeHelp: Which windows it is written for (e.g. bare, full, per shift)
kpi.denominatorHelp: Without it the ratio cannot be combined over a period.
kpi.identitiesHelp: What always holds between the columns, e.g. running + stopped = total
kpi.limitsHelp: What the computation cannot tell – one per line
kpi.diagramHelp: A diagram as text (Mermaid or plain), shown as it is
kpi.noInstances: No asset has an instance yet.
kpi.candidatesHelp: They deliver every input but have no instance.

assignment.title: Data and KPIs
assignment.help: What the asset’s interfaces deliver, where its data is published and which KPIs are computed from it.
assignment.emptyText: Name the device profile of this {{type}} to record its endpoints, where its data points are published and its KPI instances.
assignment.whoCanAct: Whoever manages the site assigns device profiles and KPI instances.
assignment.profileHelp: The kind of controller or device; its interfaces and data points apply to this asset.
assignment.profileChangeHelp: Another profile has other interfaces and data points: the endpoints, overrides and publications of this asset are removed.
assignment.firmwareHelp: The firmware this asset runs, e.g. 3.4.2
assignment.removeAllConfirm: Remove the device profile, endpoints, publications and KPI instances of “{{name}}”?
assignment.interfacesHelp: An interface delivers its data points only when it is set up and active here.
assignment.activeHelp: The interface delivers its data points on this asset.

endpointHelp.other: Where: a host, a share, a URL

assignment.overridesHelp: Data points that differ from the profile here, or that this asset does not deliver.
assignment.overrideHelp: Only what differs; empty fields keep the profile’s
assignment.availableHelp: Off: the data point exists in the profile, but not on this asset.
assignment.publicationsHelp: Which data points are published where (an IoT platform, a historian).
assignment.kpisHelp: Computation jobs of a KPI definition for this asset, with their parameters and where the result is shown.
assignment.jobHelp: The computation job’s name, unique on this asset
assignment.jobTaken: The asset has a job of this name already.
assignment.otherParamsHelp: Not parameters of the definition: a check reports them.
assignment.dashboardHelp: The Steward dashboard that shows the result
assignment.datasetHelp: The Steward dataset the result is published to
assignment.possibleHelp: KPI definitions whose every data point input this asset delivers.

checks.title: Checks
checks.description: What does not fit in the data of the {{type}} and the KPI definitions: inputs a KPI instance does not get, parameters outside their definition, ratios without their denominator.
checks.emptyText: Every KPI instance gets its inputs and parameters, and every KPI definition is complete.

codes.profile_unknown: The device profile {{profile}} does not exist (any more).
codes.kpi_unknown: The KPI definition {{kpi}} does not exist (any more).
codes.kpi_no_profile: KPI “{{kpi}}” reads data points, but the asset has no device profile.
codes.kpi_other_profile: KPI “{{kpi}}” reads data points of profile {{profile}}; the asset has profile “{{assigned}}”.
codes.kpi_point_unknown: KPI “{{kpi}}” reads data point {{point}}, which profile “{{profile}}” does not have.
codes.kpi_point_unavailable: KPI “{{kpi}}” reads data point {{point}}, which this asset does not deliver (override).
codes.kpi_interface_inactive: KPI “{{kpi}}” reads data point {{point}}, but interface “{{interface}}” is not set up as active on this asset.
codes.kpi_unit_mismatch: KPI “{{kpi}}” expects data point {{point}} in {{expected}}; this asset delivers it in {{actual}} – not convertible by a factor.
codes.kpi_unit_mismatch_convertible: KPI “{{kpi}}” expects data point {{point}} in {{expected}}; this asset delivers it in {{actual}} – convertible by a factor, but the job has to convert it.
codes.param_unknown: Parameter {{param}} is not a parameter of KPI “{{kpi}}”.
codes.param_required: Parameter {{param}} is required and has no default.
codes.ratio_no_denominator: Column {{column}} is a ratio without a denominator: it cannot be combined over a longer period.
codes.ratio_no_numerator: Column {{column}} is a ratio without a numerator.
codes.ratio_column_unknown: Ratio {{column}} names column {{ref}}, which the definition does not have.
codes.input_profile_unknown: An input names the device profile {{profile}}, which does not exist.
codes.input_point_unknown: An input names data point {{point}}, which profile “{{profile}}” does not have.

explore.title: Explore data
explore.description: Which {{type}} deliver a data point, and which KPIs an asset can have.
explore.hint: Type a data point’s id, name or address – the search goes through every device profile.
explore.nonePossible: No KPI definition: none reads only data points this asset delivers.
explore.nonePossibleNoProfile: Assign a device profile first: KPIs read its data points.

move.nodeHelp: The {{type}} moves below another {{parent}} of this site, with everything below it and its assets.
move.assetHelp: Choose the place of the {{type}} in this site's hierarchy. Everything else stays as it is.

moveEntries.devicesHelp: The devices go to another {{type}} with their ids. The data paths that name only them go along; maintenance windows, old ids and history follow.
moveEntries.collectionHelp: The data collection goes to another {{type}} with its items, sinks and Insights Hub mapping – for example when its collector now reads that {{type}}. Its data path stays.
moveEntries.otherSitesHelp: Only where you manage both sites. A device on another site leaves its VLAN and its zones.
moveEntries.collections: Data collections of the data paths
moveEntries.collectionsHelp: A collection maps its items to the data points of its asset. Leaving it keeps that mapping intact.
moveEntries.collectionsLeave: Leave them and take off their link to the data path
moveEntries.crossSite: The target is on another site: the devices leave their VLAN (and so their zones). Their addresses stay as documented.
moveEntries.crossSiteCollection: The target is on another site.
moveEntries.taken: The target has this id already
moveEntries.followsPath: Goes along: it names only devices that move
moveEntries.followsCollection: Goes along with its data path
moveEntries.leavesDataPath: Loses its link to data path {{path}}
moveEntries.unlinked_one: {{count}} data collection stays and loses its link to the data path
moveEntries.unlinked_other: {{count}} data collections stay and lose their link to the data path
moveEntries.stepUp: Moving this many entries asks you to confirm who you are.

duplicateDevice.title: Duplicate device {{name}}
duplicateDevice.help: The copy takes the device’s fields – not its host name, address, MAC address, serial number, switch port, wall outlet or CMDB port (they belong to the original) and not its checks or monitoring. On another site its VLAN stays empty.
